what_its_for: Clonidine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It is also used for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adults (Kapvay brand). Sometimes doctors prescribe it for other conditions like anxiety, hot flashes, or helping with withdrawal from certain substances.
how_to_take: Take clonidine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow extended-release (long-acting) tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. If you are using a clonidine skin patch, apply it to a clean, dry, hairless area of skin on your upper arm or chest. Change the patch every 7 days and rotate where you put it. Do not suddenly stop taking clonidine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause your blood pressure to rise quickly and dangerously.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your condition and how your body responds. For high blood pressure in adults, a common starting dose is 0.1 mg taken twice a day (morning and bedtime), and your doctor may slowly increase it if needed. For ADHD, dosing is usually based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss more than one dose of clonidine, call your doctor right away, especially if you are being treated for high blood pressure.
storage: Store clonidine tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you use the skin patch, store unused patches at room temperature and dispose of used patches by folding them in half with the sticky sides together and throwing them in the trash where children and pets cannot reach them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking clonidine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how clonidine affects you, because it can make you drowsy. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as clonidine can lower your blood pressure and make you feel dizzy or lightheaded. Avoid taking other blood pressure medicines, sleeping pills, or sedatives without telling your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: very slow or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, chest pain, shortness of breath, swelling of your hands or feet, signs of high blood pressure returning (severe headache, blurred vision, pounding heartbeat) especially if you stopped taking clonidine suddenly, or a skin rash or redness where the patch is applied. Seek emergency help (call 911) if you feel you may have taken too much clonidine.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure, clonidine usually starts lowering your blood pressure within 30 to 60 minutes after taking a dose, but it may take a few weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. For ADHD symptoms, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use before you or your child notices improvement. Keep taking it every day as directed, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Children: Clonidine for ADHD (Kapvay) is approved for children 6 years and older. Use only under close doctor supervision and never change the dose without guidance. Older adults (seniors): Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering and sedating effects of clonidine and may have a higher risk of dizziness and falls. Start low and go slow as directed by your doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using clonidine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits need to be carefully weighed. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may need to give you a lower dose, since clonidine is removed from the body through the kidneys.
